text:
maria-pm: Quick sync: Acme wants a bundled private offer that combines a committed marketplace discount + per-device rebate. They want a simple field calculator and a clean settlement flow. Can we sketch mechanics and ops guardrails?

dan-k: High level: two flows — checkout-applied credit (immediate UX) or quarter-end reconciliation (simpler ops). Which can we land by Sept?

ella-ops: Reconciliation fastest. Checkout needs SKU attachment + entitlement flags + partner co-fund ledger. Estimate checkout work = ~3 sprints. Recon approach = config + monthly settlement job.

acme-fin: Acme strongly prefers checkout so customers see the discount in real-time. They can commit to a quarterly co-fund cap to limit exposure.

phil-legal: Legal asks: cap per-account, expiry rules, audit & clawback for fraud (12 months), and explicit non-extension on renewals. Need draft appendix if we finalize bands.

josh-sales: Sales wants an "effective price" widget on SKU pages and a one-pager with 3 example deals (SMB, Mid, Enterprise). Also clarify downgrade & renewal scripts.

maria-pm: Proposed tiering (example): Starter = 12% marketplace credit + $75/device; Growth = 22% + $200; Enterprise = 35% + negotiated rebate. Gate Enterprise to manual approval.

ella-ops: Ops rules: credits expire in 6 months; device rebates expire in 9 months; partner pays gross credit (easier UX), we record partner settlement net of marketplace fees. Unused credits roll into a one-time account credit on expiry (no cash-out).

acme-fin: Can we allow mid-quarter top-ups? we need predictable cashflow.

dan-k: top-ups OK but require idempotency and partner API to push more co-fund. We'll need rate limits.

phil-legal: Add dispute window: partners have 60 days after quarter to dispute reconciliation. After that amounts are final. Also require evidence for rebates (device serials + shipment manifest).

maria-pm: Implementation checklist: (1) pricing ops -> map percent to SKU-level credit values and produce CSV, (2) partner-eng -> scope checkout wiring + reporting endpoint, (3) legal -> draft appendix, (4) marketing -> assets & messaging, (5) sales -> playbook.

josh-sales: For the calculator, please include fields: commit_amount, expected device_count, quarterly cap, net effective ARR. Example calc would help sellers close.

ella-ops: I'll make a sample SKU CSV template. Format: marketplace_sku, partner_sku, credit_usd, expiry_days. e.g.:
```
mp_sku_123, acme_dev_1, 120.00, 180
mp_sku_124, acme_dev_2, 240.00, 180
```

acme-fin: We'll provide sample shipment cadence and a proposed quarterly cap by EOD tomorrow.

phil-legal: Also include clawback language if serials are later found invalid within 12 months. Drafting now.

dan-k: Billing design question: do rebates count toward committed revenue for Dedicated contracts? ops says no — rebates are contra-revenue, not committed bookings. Confirm with finance.

maria-pm: Finance note: we should not count partner-funded discounts as recognized committed revenue. We'll flag for finance sign-off.

josh-sales: Training ask: short video + 1-pager by launch. Also a FAQ covering downgrade, returns, and credit expiry.

ell-ops: On reporting: partners get aggregated daily usage + credit consumption. Per-customer detail only under NDA. We'll expose a reconciliation feed webhook and CSV export.

recon-bot: Task created: "Prepare SKU credit CSV template" assigned to @ella-ops due in 3 business days.

maria-pm: Timeline: if numbers and caps finalized by next Tue, we can aim for a soft-launch in 6 weeks. If legal needs more time, push back. Next touch: Tue 10am PT.

acme-fin: Ok we'll try to get caps & cadence by EOD Monday. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
